# Careerden: product and public-site context

Careerden is a TypeScript open-source desktop job application tracker with a profile-aware CV creator and cover letter creator. It keeps opportunities, stages, salary and work-style context, interest, follow-ups, contacts, notes, match analysis, and application documents together from discovery through outcome. A user also maintains reusable profile details such as professional summary, skills, experience, education, projects, and certifications. In the desktop workflow, a user can submit a LinkedIn job-posting URL and the application captures source and normalized job/company information from public guest responses without connecting the user's LinkedIn account. Users can also paste job and company details manually for applications from any source. Depending on operator configuration and profile readiness, Careerden can run AI-supported requirement extraction and match analysis, then prepare editable CV and cover-letter drafts and rendered documents inside the tracked application.

## Intended workflow

1. A user installs Careerden Unplugged, which needs no account, and enters factual CV information
   in the Career Profile. AI features use a provider API key the user adds.
2. On the Base resume page, the user previews the profile as an A4 page in six built-in CV layouts
   (Classic, Editorial, Modern, Minimal, Technical, and Ledger) and sets one as the default for
   tailored CVs. There is no template upload or variable mapping.
3. In the desktop app, the user submits a LinkedIn job-posting URL and may choose output
   language and tone. Careerden queues and processes the posting while preserving source material for
   traceability. Manual application entry stores normalized pasted job/company details and optional
   company logos from other sources.
4. The captured opportunity becomes a trackable application record. The user can update its stage,
   interest, salary, work style, contacts, notes, and follow-ups. The dashboard shows active
   applications, a month calendar that marks days with follow-ups, recent activity, and the
   application pipeline. The applications list sorts by match, interest, salary, or date added.
5. AI-supported analysis compares job requirements with the supplied profile and prepares editable
   CV and cover-letter content for the Application Pack.
6. The user reviews the overview, match evidence, CV, and cover letter; edits generated content when
   needed; and applies those edits with Update pack before deciding whether to use or submit the
   documents.

Careerden is not an automatic job-application service. It does not promise employment outcomes or guarantee the accuracy of AI output. Users should verify every generated statement.

The public marketing website presents Careerden Unplugged as the edition available today. It does
not expose sign-in, signup, or browser-application links. Its `/download` page offers the Careerden
Unplugged macOS (Apple silicon and Intel) DMGs and notes that Careerden Cloud is coming soon.
Windows and Linux downloads are not offered yet.

The public pricing section presents Careerden Unplugged as free, with AI billed by the user's own
provider, and Careerden Cloud as coming soon. Cloud's planned credit model, which may change before
launch: every authenticated account receives 10 AI credits for each UTC calendar month. The $10 USD monthly subscription grants 100 credits for
each confirmed paid period, with applicable taxes potentially added at checkout. One completed
match analysis costs one credit; tracking remains available without credits. Unused credits expire
at the end of their applicable free month or paid period, and cancellation does not revoke credits
from a period already paid.

The public site links directly to the Careerden repository at
https://github.com/ErtanOzdemir/careerden. The repository is licensed under the GNU Affero General
Public License v3.0.

## Public workflow demonstration

The public landing page presents job-application tracking as the core workflow, followed by four
presentation-only steps: Add your profile, Add your first application, Review the tailored CV, and
Accept only what you can back up. A latest-features section shows the Base resume layouts and the
sortable applications list. Its screen replicas use fictional data and do not upload files, submit
jobs, or persist onboarding progress. The public copy does not claim a separate AI-regeneration action;
it describes the current edit-and-Update-pack flow.

## Careerden Unplugged

Careerden Unplugged is the desktop edition available today. It keeps the
profile, applications, follow-ups, and generated documents in a database and files on the user's
device and sends no data to a Careerden server. AI features use the user's own OpenAI, Anthropic,
Gemini, DeepSeek, or OpenRouter API key, stored with the operating system's secure storage. It has
no accounts, billing, or credits, and installs side by side with Careerden.

## Data categories described by the draft policies

The intended workflow may process account and authentication data; professional profile information; job and company source/normalized data; application workflow events and preferences; match analysis; generated and uploaded documents; rendered files; support messages; reminders; security records; and essential technical/browser data.

Production controller details, lawful-basis mapping, subprocessor names, provider regions, international transfer mechanisms, retention periods, deletion timelines, security-control descriptions, analytics choices, contact details, company identity, complete billing and refund terms, governing law, and related business/legal details are not yet confirmed. The legal pages are not published until these items pass owner and legal review, and Careerden does not claim GDPR certification or guaranteed compliance.

## Crawling guidance

Public product pages may be indexed. `/onboarding` is a legacy noindex route that redirects
to the landing-page workflow. Authenticated application routes such as login, signup, applications,
profile, templates, settings, support, and API routes should not be indexed on any deployment that
shares a host.
